One of the researchers keeps "Pterry" as a pet (I can't remember its SCP number at the moment, but it has one!). In the end, the researchers are human beings, not monsters, and I feel like this fits perfectly in that the kid has to be brought in once a month for a medical examination (which I doubt is like a normal medical physical since it's conducted by the SCP Foundation) - it isn't allowed to live an ENTIRELY normal life, and its origins will always be kept in mind by anyone who interacts with it.
Personally, I like it when the researchers do something humane for once. But I guess that's just me. Besides, I'm new, too.

item.content:encoded: This is a concept that could easily have been bland and boring, but it's done in such exquisitely squicky, well thought out detail that I don't think I'll ever be able to get it out of my mind.
